tA.text: Ledger — the BSS Admin design system

rB.text:
Hierarchy, screen by screen

Subscribers: search is the entry point (operators arrive with a name, number or BA id while on the phone). The table sits on the page, not in a card. Balance is the last, right-aligned column; an account over its credit limit is flagged in its own row.

Subscriber card: three tiers. 1) Who: name, status, mode, account actions. 2) Money: the ledger equation (ledger − reserved = available) with Top up / Adjust / Hold / Transfer beside the numbers they change. 3) What they have: tabs. Overview = products + work in flight + the last money movements, so 'why is my balance X' is answered above the fold. Every action sits next to the object it changes.

Product catalog: grouped by lifecycle, so In design → Active → Retired reads top to bottom.

Billing runs: the latest run is the headline. When it failed, its failed accounts come before history, and Retry is the only primary action on the page.

≥ 1536 px: list screens open an inspector for the selected row instead of navigating away; the card puts recent activity in a wider rail.

rD.text:
Dialog rules

S 400 confirm · M 560 form · L 760 form + preview.
Header: title, step 'n of N' when multi-step, close.
Footer: the reason or state on the left, actions on the right; primary is always last.
The primary label states the outcome with the amount ('Transfer 5.00 EUR'), never 'OK'.
Final writes get their own confirmation step with a summary and an acknowledgement checkbox; the button stays disabled until it is ticked.
Refused: the server's reason above the footer, inputs kept. Unsure: no retry button (it could double-post); Refresh reads the state back first.
